subject: a prologue cutscene scene-thumbnail icon (a dramatic story moment) for an ARPG
bestPrompt: Cinematic ARPG prologue cutscene key frame, a dramatic story moment: a lone hooded hero as a clean rim-lit dark silhouette on a windswept cliff-edge ruin at dusk, facing a colossal coherent gothic stone fortress with defined towers, buttresses and a great arched gate on the distant horizon. Hand-painted fully-rendered concept art, crisp intentional edges, confident controlled brushwork; every form carries rendered material and light, not flat silhouettes. Believable surfaces: weathered stone masonry with visible grain and moss, cloth cloak with folds, dull steel blade catching a sharp specular glint. The great gate blazes with warm emissive ember light that spills across the nearest tower faces and cliff rock and rim-lights the hero's shoulder and blade, creating crisp high-contrast focal separation. Three-plane depth: dark foreground framing, sharply-lit hero mid-ground focal point, hazy background. Dramatic key and rim lighting, one volumetric god-ray shaft through storm clouds, drifting fog, embers. Moody teal-and-orange grade, deep shadows, high contrast value hierarchy, diagonal composition. Sharp focal detail on hero and nearest tower, softer distant haze. Epic somber mood, professional AAA game concept art. Clean unmarked frame. NOT a flat vector emoji, NOT a sticker, NOT cel-shaded, NOT a photograph, NOT soft blurry mush, NOT flat color blobs. No lettering, no signature, no watermark, no logo, no UI, no border.
technique: For Lucid Origin the family is a painterly CINEMATIC KEY-FRAME (staged three-plane depth: dark foreground repoussoir -> small rim-lit hero focal point -> atmospheric architectural background), anchored by a deliberate dark-to-glow value hierarchy and a single motivated god-ray. Two Lucid-Origin-specific levers matter most: (1) TEXT/WATERMARK CONTROL is the single biggest lever early — Lucid loves to stamp a garbled fake signature (crashed i1 to 40 via cleanliness 25). Dropping brand-name style anchors ('in the style of Path of Exile 2 / Diablo IV cinematics', 'title card') and using a tight precise negative tail ('no lettering, no signature, no watermark, no logo') removed it entirely (cleanliness 25->88, score 40->66). (2) Motivated EMISSIVE light-spill (the gate glow spilling onto nearby stone + rim-lighting the hero/blade) plus explicit 'crisp intentional edges / not flat color blobs' is the correct fix direction, but it only holds the line at 66 — it does not break through. Keep the hero medium-small and simple; enlarging it (i3) invites anatomy errors (floating scabbard) and over-simplifying the scene (i4) collapses value+material back to flat silhouette-on-gradient (dropped to 58).

ceiling: MODEL-CAPPED at ~66 on Lucid Origin. Cleanliness, value hierarchy, silhouette and style-cohesion all reach 74-88 and are prompt-controllable. The wall is materialRendering (45-58) and edgeQuality (58-63): Lucid Origin renders complex cinematic scenes as flat matte color-blobs in a soft painterly haze and AI-smears gothic masonry tectonics, delivering no metal specular / cloth-fold / stone-grain read. Three separate well-composed attacks on that exact fix (i2/i3/i5) all return an identical 66 with the same finding, so >=90 is NOT reachable by prompt alone for this family on Lucid Origin at 1024 — it needs a higher-fidelity model, an img2img/detail-refiner pass, or upscale-with-detail. Prompt technique reliably wins the composition/value/cleanliness half of the rubric (baseline 22 -> 66) but cannot manufacture the rendered material fidelity the strict judge demands.
